summary: Iteration 2 backend-only testing of aiogram 3 bot at '/app/Tg Bot'. Verified new requirements: (1) English-only language audit across utils.py, keyboards.py, handlers/{admin,join,user}.py, database.py - no Banglish markers (korun/pathan/hobe/nai/dekhun/chalu/bondho/likhun/shob/apnar/amader/boshai/rakhun/shuru/shesh/koro/pathate...). (2) Telegram Premium / custom emoji support in Text Set and Broadcast: aiogram's Message.html_text renders custom_emoji entities as EMOJI; on_new_text persists html_text verbatim; text preview and broadcast confirm show 'Premium emoji: N'. (3) utils.send_html HTML parse_mode is default via DefaultBotProperties; on TelegramBadRequest it retries once with strip_tg_emoji fallback and re-raises if there were no tg-emoji tags. (4) Join handler delivers welcome via send_html, so the fallback path is exercised end-to-end. Added 11 new tests to the existing suite; total 40/40 pass. Suite still restores original approve_mode/welcome_text and cleans TEST_ rows.

minor.issue: Still uses ev.chat.id (fixed as per prev iteration) — correct now; carried over note only.

Fallback only differentiates TelegramBadRequest; a BadRequest unrelated to custom emoji on a text that happens to contain <tg-emoji> would be silently rewritten. Acceptable given log.warning emitted, but could be tightened by matching 'CUSTOM_EMOJI' in the error message.
asyncio.create_task reference not stored (noted previously). Not functional bug.

critical_code_review_comments: utils.send_html correctly checks `plain == text` before retrying and re-raises if no fallback is possible — good.
count_entities aggregates msg.entities + msg.caption_entities so Premium emoji counting works for captioned media messages in Broadcast as well.
handlers/admin.on_new_text saves message.html_text so <tg-emoji> tags are stored verbatim; render() does not touch them, so they survive to send_html.
handlers/admin.on_bc_message currently only looks at message.entities / caption_entities via count_entities; copy_message in cb_bc_go preserves all entities on Telegram's side, so this is correct.
DefaultBotProperties(parse_mode=HTML) is set in bot.py (verified via test runs) — send_message calls do not need explicit parse_mode.
English-only audit: searched handlers/*.py, utils.py, keyboards.py, database.py against a Banglish word list — zero hits.
Suggestion (optional): tighten send_html to only strip tg-emoji when the error message contains 'CUSTOM_EMOJI' to avoid masking unrelated BadRequests.
